title: Backslash-escaped characters in headers produce garbage TOC ids
spec:
This is the Python-Markdown library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -q`. With the TOC extension, a header that contains a backslash-escaped character gets an id containing the character's code point number instead of the character. ``` markdown.markdown(r'# escaped\_character', extensions=['markdown.extensions.toc']) ``` Expected: ```

escaped_character

``` Actual: ```

escaped_character

``` Another example: `# 1\. Intro` renders as `

1. Intro

`; it should be `id="1-intro"`. The header text itself is fine. An escaped character should contribute to the id exactly as the unescaped character would, so `\_` keeps the underscore and `\.` is dropped like any other punctuation.
acceptance: Other backslash escapes in headers (e.g. `\.`) produce ids as if the character were unescaped
